paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Ethan sings about the LORD's loving devotion and faithfulness from start to finish, and he sings it while the king's throne is on the ground. God swore to David, "I will not lie to David" (Psalm 89:35), and then Ethan looks around and it sure doesn't look like it. So he does something brave and tells God exactly how it looks.

That's the part I want you to hold onto. Ethan asks, "How long, O LORD?" (Psalm 89:46) and "Where, O Lord, is Your loving devotion of old, which You faithfully swore to David?" (Psalm 89:49). I spent years in the back of a junk drawer asking some version of that, so I'm not about to tell you to stuff those feelings down. The psalm shows that honest questions and real trust can sit in the same song.

And look at how Ethan ends it: "Blessed be the LORD forever! Amen and amen." (Psalm 89:52). Nothing on the ground has changed yet, but he blesses the LORD anyway, because he's looking at who God is and what God swore. So when your own situation looks like rubble, baker, bring the whole honest mess to God and keep your eyes on His promise. I think that's what Ethan's doing, and I'd like to be as brave as he is, on my best day.
